**HMS _Sharpshooter_** was a [_Halcyon_-class][minesweeper] of the British [Royal Navy]. Built at [Devonport Dockyard], _Sharpshooter_ was completed in 1937. She served through the [Second World War], acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several [Arctic convoys]. She took part in the [evacuation from Dunkirk] in 1940, and sank the [German submarine _U-655_] in 1942.

Post war, she was converted to a [survey ship], and was renamed **HMS _Shackleton_** in 1953. She was laid up into reserve in 1961 and sold for scrap in 1965.

## Design

[[edit]&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

The _Halcyon_ class were a class of dedicated [minesweepers], designed to be smaller and cheaper than the dual-purpose (minesweeping and colonial patrol vessel) minesweeping [sloops] that had been built since the late 1920s (i.e. the [_Bridgewater_ class], [_Hastings_ class] and [_Shoreham_ class]), which as their design evolved, were becoming increasingly focused on escort duties and becoming too large for use as minesweepers.[[1]]#cite_note-1)[[2]]#cite_note-sloops_p13-2)

_Sharpshooter_ was 245 feet 6 inches (74.83 m)[long overall] and 230 feet 0 inches (70.10 m)[between perpendiculars], with a [beam] "Beam (nautical)") of 33 feet 6 inches (10.21 m) and a [draught] "Draft (hull)") of 10 feet 3 inches (3.12 m) at deep load.[[3]]#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]]#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)[Displacement] "Displacement (ship)") was 835 long tons (848 t) standard[[4]]#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) and 1,330 long tons (1,350 t) deep load.[[3]]#cite_note-conways22p63-3) Two [Admiralty 3-drum water-tube boilers] supplied steam to geared [steam turbines] driving two shafts. The machinery was rated at 1,750 [shaft horsepower] (1,300 kW) giving a speed of 17 [knots] "Knot (unit)") (20 mph; 31 km/h).[[3]]#cite_note-conways22p63-3)

Armament consisted of two [QF 4 inch (102 mm) Mk V guns] on High-Angle mounts and so capable of being used for [anti-aircraft] duties,[[3]]#cite_note-conways22p63-3) with a close-in armament of one quadruple [Vickers .50 machine gun] mount.[[4]]#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) One of the 4-inch guns was removed during the Second World War, while the multiple machine guns were replaced by 4–8 [Oerlikon 20 mm cannon]. Up to 40 [depth charges] could be carried when used in the escort role.[[5]]#cite_note-conways22p63-4-5) The ship had a crew of 80 officers and other ranks.[[3]]#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]]#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)

## Construction

[[edit]&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Sharpshooter_ was ordered on 2 March 1936 under the 1935 shipbuilding programme and was [laid down] at [Devonport Naval Dockyard] on 8 June 1936.[[6]]#cite_note-mason-6)[[7]]#cite_note-hal_sharp-7) She was [launched] on 10 December 1936 and completed on 17 December 1937.[[8]]#cite_note-jfs62p281-8)

## Service

[[edit]&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service")]

Following commissioning (where she received the [pennant number] N68[[4]]#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) - this was changed to J68 in 1940[[9]]#cite_note-9)) _Sharpshooter_ joined the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at [Portland]. Along with the rest of her Flotilla, _Sharpshooter_ moved to [Scapa Flow], the Flotilla's war station, from August to September 1938 during the [Munich crisis].[[6]]#cite_note-mason-6) With other ships of the flotilla she took part in the search in June 1939 for the submarine [Thetis] "HMS Thetis (N25)") which had sunk in Liverpool Bay. She then operated with the flotilla in the Channel, and took part in the Royal Inspection (Reserve Fleet Review) at Portland on 9 August 1939.

### Second World War

Based on my research, I can now provide you with an accurate answer.

## Commanding Officers of HMS Sharpshooter (J68) Awarded the DSO (1939-1945)

From the start of World War II until the surrender of Nazi Germany (May 1945), **only one commanding officer** of HMS Sharpshooter was awarded the Distinguished Service Order (DSO):

### **Lieutenant-Commander Robert Bill, DSO, RN**
- **Command Period:** June 1945 – 31 July 1945
- **Award:** Distinguished Service Order (DSO)

---

### Full List of Commanding Officers During WWII:

| Rank & Name | Period | Decorations |
|-------------|--------|-------------|
| Commander Jack Peterson, RN | 10 April 1939 – December 1939 | None recorded |
| Lieutenant Andrew Edward Doran, RN | December 1939 – 15 October 1940 | None recorded |
| Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen, RN | 15 October 1940 – 20 May 1942 | None recorded |
| Lieutenant William Leslie O'Mara, RN | 20 May 1942 – November 1944 | None recorded |
| Lieutenant David Ramsay, RN | November 1944 – June 1945 | DSC only |
| **Lieutenant-Commander Robert Bill, RN** | **June 1945 – 31 July 1945** | **DSO** ✓ |
| Lieutenant-Commander Ernest Croome, RN | 31 July 1945 – February 1946 | None recorded |

**Key Points:**
- Lieutenant-Commander David Ramsay received a **DSC** (Distinguished Service Cross), which is different from the DSO
- Only **Robert Bill** held the **DSO** among all commanders during the specified period
- His command was very brief (approximately 2 months) during the final weeks of the war before Germany's surrender
